extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in entertainment, stand-up comedy, and celebrity controversy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative statements relevant to stand-up comedians about crafting material, handling controversial jokes, responding to backlash, and finding an audience. Emphasizes intent, vulnerability, and certain off-limit topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic violence is not funny
rubrics_metrics.description: "Domestic violence is not funny, ever, ever, on any comedy special ever."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an explicit moral/professional prohibition in this article: domestic violence should be treated as off-limits material for comedy specials. The story contrasts this statement with the earlier controversial joke and Rife's later clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent as the primary evaluative criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: "The way I look at it is, as a comedian everything comes down to intent... everything that leaves my mouth on stage is purely with the intention of making people laugh."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames comic material's acceptability around the performer’s intent to make people laugh rather than malicious intent. The article records the comedian using intent as a defense, but also shows that intent may not prevent backlash in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be vulnerable on stage to find your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "You have to go out there and do your comedy and just lay it all out there, vulnerably, to find your audience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for performers to present authentic, personal material and test responses live to identify and build their audience. Encourages risk-taking and openness as part of craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect varied audience tastes and the risk of offending
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked whether he’s worried about offending audiences with his darker material, Rife replied: "You don’t know what other people are into and that’s why you have to go out there..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that darker or provocative material will not suit all audiences; comedians should anticipate differing reactions and possible criticism when working in such territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering; prioritize authenticity over demographic-targeted pandering
rubrics_metrics.description: "Natural Selection was 'way more for guys'... One thing I wanted to tackle in this special was showing people that, despite what you think about me online, I don’t pander my career to women."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions an approach of not tailoring material solely to placate a particular demographic. This is framed as an artistic/professional stance but may itself be controversial or risky for audience relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dismissive or provocative responses to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Rife responded to criticism with an Instagram Story linking to a website selling helmets for people with special needs, and later joked about it onstage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents this as an example of a provocative, dismissive reaction to backlash; such responses can escalate controversy and be seen as insensitive or inflammatory (an anti-pattern).
